answer: Every solstice the keeper checks the noon shadow against the line carved in the calibration stone, and the reading is entered in the station book. A nadir stone cut in a workshop fails the check: at the dawn of the shadow the line must fall where the sun puts it, and a workshop line is always a finger off. Forging the stone means carving a new dial, watching 60 noons and paying 7,600, and the comet mark on the stone is sealed in wax yearly, so a dial whose line was never tested is pulled from the garden.
